findings.evidence: `rg -n "realOperator_of_nonneg|ofBounded_realOperator" code/TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups` shows `ExponentialShift.lean:96 theorem expShift_realOperator_of_nonneg ... (ht : 0 ≤ t)` and `BoundedGenerator.lean:94 theorem ofBounded_realOperator ... (ht : 0 ≤ t)`. Mathlib naming conventions say hypotheses are separated with `of`, and adjacent consistency takes priority.
findings.fix: Rename it to `ofBounded_realOperator_of_nonneg` and update its uses; this matches the existing nearby names `expShift_realOperator_of_nonneg` and `expShift_realOperator_apply_of_nonneg`.
findings.issue: `ofBounded_realOperator` states the real-time formula only under `ht : 0 ≤ t`, but the name does not record this restriction, so it reads like an unconditional formula for `realOperator` on all real times.

summary: One public theorem name omits a necessary hypothesis and conflicts with adjacent semigroup naming for real-time operators.
